batchName: Empire: The Five Good Emperors (AD 96-192) - Easy Batch 1

questions.question: Dacia, the kingdom Trajan conquered, lay mostly in which modern country?
questions.explanation: Dacia lay north of the lower Danube in what is now Romania. Romanians still honour Trajan as a founder of their nation.
questions.sourceQuote: Dacia, a powerful kingdom north of the lower Danube in what is now Romania, had troubled Rome for years.

questions.question: Which philosophy did Marcus Aurelius devotedly follow?
questions.explanation: Marcus was a devoted Stoic, a philosophy of self-control and duty. He took power reluctantly in 161.
questions.sourceQuote: Marcus Aurelius, born in Rome in 121 and the adopted heir of Antoninus Pius, was a devoted Stoic, follower of a philosophy of self-control and duty.

questions.question: What final password did the dying Antoninus Pius give the officer of the night watch?
questions.explanation: On 7 March 161 Antoninus handed the state to Marcus and gave the password 'equanimity' (aequanimitas). He was dying of a fever at his country estate.
questions.sourceQuote: On 7 March 161, dying of a fever at his country estate, he handed the state to Marcus and gave the officer of the night watch his final password: 'equanimity' (*aequanimitas*).

questions.question: How was Hadrian connected to Trajan before becoming emperor?
options: He was Nerva's grandson and heir
He was Trajan's eldest son by birth
He was Trajan's ward and married his grandniece
questions.explanation: Orphaned at ten, Hadrian became Trajan's ward and later married his grandniece. Both men came from the Spanish town of Italica.
questions.sourceQuote: Orphaned at ten, he became Trajan's ward and later married Trajan's grandniece.

questions.question: What was the alimenta, which Trajan formalised?
options: A pension fund for retired legionaries
A tax on grain imports from Egypt
A welfare scheme for poor children in Italy
questions.explanation: The alimenta gave cash, food and schooling to orphans and poor children across Italy. Trajan was also a lavish builder in Rome.
questions.sourceQuote: He formalised the *alimenta*, a welfare scheme giving cash, food and schooling to orphans and poor children across Italy.

questions.question: What is the name now given to the private notes Marcus Aurelius wrote in camp?
questions.explanation: Marcus wrote the Meditations in Greek between 170 and 180 while campaigning. They are still widely read.
questions.sourceQuote: In camp between 170 and 180 Marcus wrote, in Greek, the private notes now called the Meditations, still widely read.

questions.question: How did Antoninus earn the name Pius, 'the dutiful'?
options: By caring for his aged father in public
By insisting the Senate declare Hadrian a god
By rebuilding the temples of Italy
questions.explanation: Antoninus threatened to refuse the throne unless the reluctant Senate deified Hadrian. The senators gave way and honoured his loyalty with the name Pius.
questions.sourceQuote: The senators gave way and honoured his loyalty with the name Pius, 'the dutiful'.

questions.question: After the Jewish revolt, Jerusalem was rebuilt as a Greek-style city under what name?
questions.explanation: Jerusalem was rebuilt as Aelia Capitolina. At the same time the province of Judaea was renamed Syria Palaestina.
questions.sourceQuote: Judaea was renamed Syria Palaestina, and Jerusalem was rebuilt as a Greek-style city called Aelia Capitolina.

questions.question: Under which emperor did the Roman Empire reach its greatest size?
questions.explanation: Trajan's eastern conquests pushed the empire to its greatest extent. The gains did not last, as revolts broke out across Mesopotamia.
questions.sourceQuote: Under Trajan the empire reached its greatest size.

questions.question: Emperor Trajan was born in Italica, a Roman town near which modern city?
questions.explanation: Trajan was born in Italica, near modern Seville in southern Spain. The town had been settled by Italian veterans.
questions.sourceQuote: That general was Trajan, born in AD 53 (or perhaps 56) in Italica, a Roman town near modern Seville in southern Spain that had been settled by Italian veterans.
